items.title: Add a scope_glob_overlap degradation kind to resolveWaveSafety, computed at the storyRef() call site from active parallel peers' write-sets via computeWriteSet + globsOverlap
items.context: core/lattice-parallel-wave.ts: resolveWaveSafety is a pure projector (does not read scope contracts). At the storyRef() call site, for each ACTIVE non-terminal peer that also asserts parallelSafe='yes', compute this story's and the peer's write-set via computeWriteSet(scopeContract) and run globsOverlap; pass the overlap results into resolveWaveSafety as a new parameter; emit a 'scope_glob_overlap' degradation (severity 'warn', authorityImpact 'none', visible true) via the existing schedulingDegradation() factory naming the peer + an example colliding pair. None when disjoint or peer terminal.

happy.desc: computeScopeGlobOverlaps(self parallelSafe=yes writeSet [core/foo.ts], peers [{B-p1, phase DEV, parallelSafe yes, writeSet [core/foo.ts]}]) -> one overlap naming B-p1 with pairExample core/foo.ts; WHY: the core positive case — a real write-set collision with an active parallel peer is surfaced

the overlap result, fed into resolveWaveSafety, produces a ParallelWaveDegradation with capability scope_glob_overlap, severity warn, visible true, authorityImpact none, reason naming the peer + pair; WHY: proves the degradation kind is emitted via schedulingDegradation with the right shape

edge.desc: self.parallelSafe!=yes (undefined or no) -> computeScopeGlobOverlaps returns [] even with an overlapping active parallel peer; WHY: only a story ASSERTING parallel can falsely assert it
peer in TERMINAL_PHASES (DONE/DISCARDED) -> no overlap emitted even with identical write-set; WHY: terminal peers are not concurrent, must not generate noise
peer with parallelSafe!=yes -> no overlap; and self vs self (same storyId) skipped; WHY: only active parallel peers count, never self
disjoint write-sets (core/foo.ts vs core/bar.ts) -> no overlap; WHY: independence provable, no false positive

adversarial.desc: a peer whose scope contract is null/missing is skipped when building peer write-sets (call-site filters null) -> no throw, no overlap for that peer; WHY: legacy stories lacking a contract must not crash the wave projection
multiple active parallel peers each overlapping -> one degradation per peer, each naming the correct peer + pair; WHY: proves per-peer fan-out, no dedup loss

verificationEvidence.note: smoke asserts computeScopeGlobOverlaps(self parallelSafe=yes [core/foo.ts], peers [{B-p1 DEV yes [core/foo.ts]}]) returns one overlap naming B-p1 with the colliding pair example.

smoke asserts scopeGlobOverlapDegradations('B-self',[{B-p1,...}]) returns one ParallelWaveDegradation with capability scope_glob_overlap, severity warn, visible true, authorityImpact none, id containing scope-glob-overlap+b-p1, reason naming the peer — the degradation resolveWaveSafety emits.
smoke asserts self.parallelSafe!=='yes' (undefined/no) returns [] even with an overlapping active parallel peer.
smoke asserts a TERMINAL_PHASES peer (phase DONE) yields no overlap even with identical write-set.
smoke asserts a peer with parallelSafe!=='yes' yields no overlap, and self-vs-self (same storyId) is skipped.
smoke asserts disjoint write-sets (core/foo.ts vs core/bar.ts) yield no overlap.
smoke models a null/missing-contract peer by omitting it from the peers list (call-site filters null) -> no throw, no overlap for that peer.
smoke asserts multiple overlapping active parallel peers yield one degradation entry per peer naming the correct peer+pair (per-peer fan-out).

items.title: Inject evaluateDecompositionGate().advisories into story_review issues[] at severity 'advisory' (non-blocking, never raises blockerCount)
items.context: handlers/story-review.ts: load peers via store.listStoryIds()+readStory(), contracts via store.readScopeContract() (null-tolerant; §4.8 handles a missing peer contract inside the gate), cfg via resolveAuditConfig(...).parallelGate; call evaluateDecompositionGate(story, peers, contracts, cfg) and push each advisories[] entry as {type:'decomposition_advisory', severity:'advisory', message}. Only advisories — the gate's block field is intentionally ignored at REVIEW (enforcement is Story 5). blockerCount = issues.filter(i=>i.severity==='blocker').length, so advisories never block REVIEW or affect the signed review.json.

happy.desc: decompositionAdvisoryIssues(story parallelSafe=yes overlapping an active parallel peer, peers, contracts, cfg) returns issues each {type: decomposition_advisory, severity: advisory, message: <non-empty gate advisory>}; WHY: the gate advisories are surfaced at REVIEW as advisory-severity issues
the returned issues, appended to a sample issues[] containing one blocker, leave blockerCount (filter severity===blocker) unchanged; WHY: proves advisories never raise blockerCount

edge.desc: a story+peers configuration where evaluateDecompositionGate returns advisories=[] -> decompositionAdvisoryIssues returns []; WHY: no advisory, no issue injected

evaluateDecompositionGate returns a non-null block (e.g. overlap_declared_parallel) AND advisories -> only the advisories become issues; the block field is NOT turned into a blocker issue; WHY: enforcement is Story 5; REVIEW must surface advisories only

adversarial.desc: a peer with a missing/unreadable contract (not in the contracts Map) -> decompositionAdvisoryIssues does not throw (evaluateDecompositionGate handles peer-unreadable per §4.8); WHY: must not crash REVIEW on legacy peers
every issue produced has severity exactly advisory (never blocker) and type decomposition_advisory; WHY: a typo to blocker would silently break the non-blocking contract

verificationEvidence.note: smoke asserts decompositionAdvisoryIssues over a story+peer+contracts yielding gate advisories returns issues each {type decomposition_advisory, severity advisory, message non-empty}.
smoke appends the produced issues to an issues[] containing one blocker and asserts blockerCount (filter severity===blocker) is unchanged.
smoke asserts a config where evaluateDecompositionGate returns advisories=[] yields decompositionAdvisoryIssues -> [].
smoke asserts when the gate also returns a non-null block, only the advisories become issues; the block field is NOT turned into a blocker issue.
smoke asserts a peer with a missing contract (absent from the contracts Map) does not throw (gate handles peer-unreadable per §4.8).
smoke asserts every produced issue has severity exactly 'advisory' and type 'decomposition_advisory' (never blocker).
